reasoning: The code fact is real -- pybridge.py has no runtime duckdb version/platform check (grep of the file confirms no reference to duckdb.__version__ or any guard) and hardcodes id(conn)+16 (pybridge.py:59) then cpp_obj_p+32 (pybridge.py:62), while the pin (pyproject.toml duckdb>=1.3.2,<1.6) permits 1.4.x/1.5.x. But the finding's specific risk claim -- that an in-range release such as 1.4.x/1.5.x could silently change the layout so 'cpp_obj_p+32 reads a wrong word' -- is directly contradicted by conclusive evidence gathered two ways. (1) CI: .github/workflows/numbduck_ci.yml:24 runs the full pytest suite (no addopts/conftest filtering, confirmed no conftest.py exists) across duckdb-version matrix [1.3.2, 1.4.0, 1.5.1] on ubuntu-latest, ubuntu-24.04-arm, and windows-latest; this exercises all three call sites of extract_connection_ptr in test/test_ducklib.py (lines 2569, 2626, 2724, including the SELECT-1-validated path). The latest main run (28539203573, merge of PR #49, 2026-07-01) is GREEN 51/51 jobs, i.e. every matrix cell -- covering 1.4.0 and 1.5.1 on three OS/arch combos -- passed. (2) Direct reproduction performed here: installed duckdb 1.3.2, 1.4.0, and 1.5.1 into isolated pip --target dirs on this Linux x86-64 host and called numbduck.pybridge.extract_connection_ptr(conn) directly against each. All three returned a valid, C-API-validated Connection* (the function's own internal 'SELECT 1' check passed) with no error: 1.3.2 -> 0x3d17d730, 1.4.0 -> 0x1c610070, 1.5.1 -> 0x2e2c6740. This empirically confirms the id(conn)+16 / cpp_obj_p+32 offsets are stable across the entire currently-pinned-and-tested duckdb range on Linux x86-64, not merely 1.3.2 as the docstring conservatively claims. The numbox sibling-contract analogy (pysqlite_bridge.libraries_coordinated()) is also an imperfect match: that gate detects two divergent *already-loaded* libsqlite3 copies (the macOS dyld-shared-cache scenario), a materially different failure mode from single-library cross-release ABI drift, so it doesn't establish that an equivalent guard is straightforwardly applicable here. Given the claimed 'high' severity rests entirely on speculative breakage for 1.4.x/1.5.x that has now been shown not to occur (both via exhaustive CI and independent direct reproduction), the finding as characterized is refuted. What legitimately remains is a much narrower, lower-value hardening point: (a) no macOS runner exists in the CI matrix at all (arch: ubuntu-latest/ubuntu-24.04-arm/windows-latest only), so the docstring's 'Linux x86-64/libstdc++' scope is honest and macOS is genuinely untested -- but that is a platform-coverage gap, not the duckdb-version-drift risk the finding names; and (b) a defense-in-depth version/platform assertion is still reasonable to add proactively for versions released after this review. Neither rises to 'high severity active bug'; at most a 'low' severity, nice-to-have hardening recommendation.
